subject: physics
question_text: The percentage errors in the mass and the speed are 2% and 3% respectively. What is the maximum error in the kinetic energy calculated using these quantities?

verification.note: Unit 2 has NO Short Answer or Long Answer section in EITHER source book — the Fastrack (pp.4-5) and the TSBIE Basic Learning Material (pp.2-3) both list Very Short Answer questions only. So every Unit 2 card is a 2-mark VSAQ and no 8-mark form is invented. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The relation used
lines: Kinetic energy K = ½ m v², so K ∝ m v².
For a maximum error the terms are added:
steps.why: The worst case is when both errors push the answer the same way, so the maximum is found by adding, never by subtracting.
common_mistakes: Subtracting the two errors, which gives the smallest error rather than the maximum.
Forgetting the factor 2 on the speed term.

recall.must_convey: That kinetic energy goes as m v squared, so the error is the mass error plus twice the speed error.

steps.memory_tip: v is squared, so its error is doubled. Maximum error means ADD.
steps.margin_note: The word "maximum" is why the terms add.

steps.label: The answer
steps.why: The speed contributes 6 of the 8 percent, which shows why a careful speed measurement matters more here than a careful mass measurement.
common_mistakes: Getting 5% by leaving out the factor 2.

recall.must_convey: That the maximum error in the kinetic energy is eight percent.

steps.memory_tip: 2% + 6% = 8%. The 6 is the doubled speed error.
steps.margin_note: Show the 2 × 3% step so the 6% is visible.

insider_note: Speed is squared, so its error doubles. Errors always add for a maximum — never subtract.
